reader.requirement: At 1985, an indexed WRITE must refuse (invalid key, '22') a record whose ALTERNATE RECORD KEY value duplicates a stored one unless that key carries DUPLICATES, and for a DUPLICATES key the records sharing a value must be retrieved sequentially (READ NEXT under that key of reference) in the order they were released, across every access mode (sequential, random, dynamic), open mode (OUTPUT, I-O, EXTEND) and file session; the witnesses cover only dynamic access in one OUTPUT session (l1c38) plus survival across CLOSE (pb2693).

edition-consulted.switches: the FILE-CONTROL key-clause rule table: below 2002 the 2023 rows plus the 1985 rows (e.g. §1985:IX.2.5.3 SR2, alternate key must be alphanumeric: COBOL0863) - a syntax screen on the key, not GR16's semantics
DialectBehavior.IndexedDuplicateKeyStatusSequentialOnly: at 1985 a random READ of a duplicate set also answers '02' (READ status, not GR16's order)

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|CobolVersion|DialectBehavior over IndexedConnector.cs, KeyedStore.cs, Store/KeyOrders.cs, RecordFraming.cs: WRITE/ReleaseOrdinals/Release/CompositeKeyOrder consult no edition; the release-ordinal ordering is one arm for every edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the duplicate-order mechanism (one fresh release ordinal stamped in every key slot, composite key part+ordinal) is edition-free; only the key's legal category (1985 alphanumeric only) and READ's random '02' differ
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1c38 covers dynamic access in one OUTPUT session; not exercised there: ACCESS SEQUENTIAL, OPEN EXTEND and OPEN I-O adding to an existing duplicate set, variable-length (RECORD VARYING / ODO) records

probes.printed: W1 00/W2 02/W3 00/W4 IK 22 (AU dup, no DUPLICATES)/W5 02/W6 02/W7 02 (OPEN I-O second session, dynamic, prime order P01<P05..); READ NEXT by AN: P50 AA 02, P20 AA 02, P01 AA 02, P30 AA 00, P90 BB 02, P99 BB 00, EOF
probes.expected: GR16: dup under DUPLICATES key retrieved in release order (P50,P20,P01,P30 not prime order); non-DUPLICATES alternate dup refused with invalid key '22'; '02' on write per §1985:IX.1.3.4 status 02 item 2

probes.printed: error COBOL0863: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY 'AN' is a category-numeric item; data-name-1 must be defined as a data item of the category alphanumeric (ANSI §1985:IX.2.5.3 SR2)
probes.expected: 1985 arm: a numeric alternate key (legal from 2002) is refused

probes.printed: RECORD VARYING 6..20 + ODO, ACCESS SEQUENTIAL: W1 00/W2 02/W3 00/W4 02, OPEN EXTEND W5 02; START AD=ZZ, READ NEXT: A10 ZZ 09 02, A20 ZZ 07 02, A40 ZZ 08 02, A50 ZZ 07 00, EOF; failed OPEN INPUT of absent file G -> 35, WRITE then -> 48
probes.expected: release order within ZZ including the EXTEND record last, lengths preserved; WRITE on a file not open for output is unsuccessful

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR16  (4.9.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR16

reader.notes: WRITE stamps one fresh release ordinal into every key slot (ReleaseOrdinals) and alternate trees are keyed by value+ordinal (CompositeKeyOrder), so a duplicate set reads back in release order regardless of prime order, access mode, open mode or session. The non-DUPLICATES refusal is Duplicates() -> '22'. No edition arm on this path; probes at --std 85 all printed the release order.

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-011/c1/r1.cob (--std 85, DYNAMIC, two DUPLICATES alt keys, OPEN OUTPUT then I-O): DELETE of the first of the AN set then WRITE of the same record puts it last; REWRITE changing AM only keeps AN order and moves the record last in AM's set; random READ KEY IS AN returns the first released (P20), READ NEXT continues P40,P50,P10 = release order; AM set P40,P50,P20,P10 = release order. c3.cob: SUPPRESS WHEN refused at 85 (COBOL0900); c2.cob RECORD KEY WITH DUPLICATES refused (COBOL1970); 'ALTERNATE KEY' without RECORD refused (1985 format underlines RECORD, spec line 18688). Indexed key order is native at 85 (ResolveFileCollating: no clause -> native; §1985 Fixed File Attributes). OK  §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR16 the text is in GR16; OK  §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR17 the text is in GR17.
